title: Retail technology predictions for 2027
summary: From agentic commerce to AI-agent security, see five 2027 retail technology predictions and why trusted information is the foundation for AI success.
body_markdown:
Two years of generative AI pilots, retail media networks and store-level computer vision are colliding with operational reality: thin margins, volatile supply chains, persistent theft and fraud, and shoppers who expect every channel to work. The winners will not have the most AI demos. They will have the information foundation to make AI trustworthy, connected and secure.


Five retail technology trends for 2027 stand out: agentic commerce, conversational engagement, network-based supply chain visibility, AI-agent security and continuous performance engineering. Across all five, competitive advantage will come from trusted, connected and secure information.


## 1. Agentic commerce turns product content into a strategic asset


**Prediction:** More retailers will make product data quality an executive-level KPI in 2027.


Shoppers are delegating searching, comparing and buying to AI agents;[Deloitte reports that more than a third already use AI to complete purchases](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/industries/consumer/articles/agentic-commerce-ai-in-retail.html) (Deloitte, *The future of AI in retail* , July 22, 2026). The first reader of a product page is increasingly a machine, and machines reward data that is complete, structured and current. Incomplete attributes mean invisibility. In 2027, retailers will treat product content, policies and brand assets as governed enterprise information, not marketing collateral.[OpenText™ Content Cloud](https://www.opentext.com/products/content-cloud) , including[OpenText™ Core Content Management](https://www.opentext.com/products/core-content-management) and[OpenText™ Content Aviator™](https://www.opentext.com/aviator-ai/content-aviator) , helps retailers capture, govern and enrich content across systems such as SAP, Microsoft and Salesforce, then apply AI in context.


## 2. Conversations become the new storefront


**Prediction:** Retailers consolidate engagement tooling onto fewer, AI-ready platforms.


Personalization is moving from segmented campaigns to real-time, two-way conversations across messaging, web, mobile and the contact center, with AI as the new interface.[Deloitte found that 67% of surveyed retail executives expected AI-driven personalization capabilities within a year](https://www.deloitte.com/global/en/Industries/consumer/perspectives/global-retail-industry-outlook.html) (Deloitte, *2026 Global Retail Industry Outlook* , January 8, 2026; survey of 330 retail executives). Retail media raises the stakes, because monetizing first-party data demands relevance, measurement and consent discipline. The obstacle is orchestration: most retailers run engagement on fragmented stacks.[OpenText™ Experience Cloud](https://www.opentext.com/products/experience-cloud) unifies communications, content, messaging, customer data and contact center analytics so brand voice and context travel with the customer.


## 3. Network-based visibility redefines supply chains and returns


**Prediction:** Network-based visibility, not ERP-centric planning, becomes the basis for inventory and returns decisions.


Geopolitical risk, regionalization and tariff volatility keep supply chain resilience on the board agenda, while returns and reverse logistics squeeze margins and invite fraud. Both problems share a root cause: partners connected through brittle, one-off integrations.[OpenText™ Business Network Cloud](https://www.opentext.com/products/business-network-cloud) , including[OpenText™ Trading Grid™](https://www.opentext.com/products/trading-grid) , provides a single platform to onboard suppliers, carriers and logistics partners across electronic data interchange (EDI) and APIs, automate procure-to-pay, track shipments and support e-Invoicing compliance. That network data also becomes the best fuel for AI forecasting.


## 4. Security extends to AI agents, fraud and the store edge


**Prediction:** AI-agent identity is expected to become a standard procurement requirement, while security teams converge with fraud and loss prevention.


[EY’s 2026 CEO Outlook](https://www.ey.com/en_gl/insights/retail/how-retail-will-need-to-adapt-for-different-agentic-futures) found that 80% of surveyed retail leaders planned to increase AI investment, yet 24% identified cybersecurity and data privacy as a top risk (EY, *How retail will need to adapt for different agentic futures* , August 21, 2026, citing the May 2026 EY CEO Outlook Survey). Industry attention is shifting toward AI-agent identity and automated exposure remediation, signaling that every agent will need an identity, permissions and an audit trail. Add point-of-sale endpoints, payment data, return fraud and organized retail crime, and security becomes inseparable from operations.[OpenText™ Cybersecurity Cloud](https://www.opentext.com/products/cybersecurity-cloud) brings threat detection and response, identity and access, data protection, application security and endpoint management into one portfolio.


## 5. Performance and resilience are engineered, not hoped for


**Prediction:** Performance testing shifts left into every release, and load profiles begin to include agent traffic.


Peak season is no longer a season. Social-driven spikes, flash promotions and agent-generated traffic stress storefronts year-round, while every new API and AI service adds a potential failure point. Retailers will move from hoping systems hold up to engineering them for resilience.[OpenText™ DevOps Cloud](https://www.opentext.com/products/devops-cloud) supports intelligent performance and load testing before launch, and[OpenText™ Software Delivery Aviator™](https://www.opentext.com/aviator-ai/devops-aviator) brings AI into the delivery lifecycle.[OpenText™ Observability and Service Management](https://www.opentext.com/products/observability-service-management-cloud) , including[OpenText™ AI Operations Management](https://www.opentext.com/products/ai-operations-management) , then keeps stores and corporate teams running with AI operations (AIOps), self-service and incident automation.


## The common thread


None of these trends are about technology for its own sake. Each depends on trusted information: governed content, connected partners, secure identities and resilient systems. AI will amplify whatever foundation it sits on, for better or worse. My advice for 2027 planning is to fund the foundation first, then scale the intelligence on top of it.
